### Observed differences

- Activity A01 disappeared from execution. In the earlier window it ran in every one of the 200 traces, about 3.5 times per trace, with repeated occurrences in about 74 in 100 traces, typically around one third into the trace; in the later window it appears in 0 of 200 traces, and its outgoing transitions (702 observed earlier) are gone. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]
- The hand-over into A01 was rerouted. Earlier, about 88 in 100 of A03's observed outgoing transitions went to A01, and about 85 in 100 of A05's; in the later window none do. A03 now leads to A10 (about 42 in 100), A09 (about 39) and A08 (about 19); A05 now leads to A09 (about 41), A10 (about 38) and A08 (about 21). [DIR002, DIR003]
- A01's former partners now run without it. A09, A08 and A10 each co-occurred with A01 in all earlier traces (mostly interleaved or repeated with it, about 74–86 in 100) and still occur in all later traces, but now never with A01. A03 and A05, which earlier appeared only alongside A01 (in about 47 and 65 in 100 traces), occur at similar rates in the later window (about 46% and 67% of traces) but never together with A01; about 54% and 33% of later traces contain neither of them nor A01. [REL004, REL003, REL005, REL001, REL002]
- The downstream activities sit closer together in event positions. The share of occurrences at distance 1 rose for A03–A10 (about 3 to 23 in 100), A03–A09 (about 3 to 20), A05–A09 (about 3 to 13) and A05–A10 (about 3 to 12), while the frequent 4-step separation from A08 largely vanished (A03–A08: about 28 to under 1 in 100; A05–A08: about 19 to under 1). These are event-position distances within five steps, not clock times. [LAG003, LAG002, LAG005, LAG006, LAG001, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 was removed from the process, or is no longer executed, and that the flow which previously passed through it now runs directly from A03 and A05 to A10, A09 and A08. The disappearance is observed directly (participation 100% to 0 of 200 traces; outgoing transitions 702 to 0), the rerouting is observed directly on A03's and A05's outgoing transitions, and the relational items show A01's former partners now executing in traces without it while A03 and A05 kept their previous participation levels. This is unlikely to be a sampling artefact: 17 control-flow items qualified where fewer than 1 (0.26) would be expected if nothing had changed, and every item's difference exceeds 99.5% of random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]

Limitations: zero participation only shows that A01 was not observed in the later sample, so removal from the process cannot be distinguished from A01 remaining in place but never being executed; the internal order among A10, A09 and A08 after A03/A05 is known only as shares over outgoing transitions and position distances, not as clock-time behaviour; and many items describe the same underlying difference, so they are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG003]

Other differences: the A08–A09 distance profile shifted mildly in the opposite direction (distance 1 down from about 14 to 7 in 100, distance 4 up from about 4 to 7), a small redistribution whose relation to the rerouting is not resolved by the evidence. [LAG007]
